public_payload.normalized_proposition: Unless hyperscalers reach at least $2 trillion in annual AI revenue by 2030, their AI capex will have been wasted.
conditions: if hyperscalers fail to reach $2 trillion annual AI revenue by 2030

statement.excerpt: And now the rest of the world has caught up to what I’ve been saying since October 2025 — that hyperscalers need at least $2 trillion in annual AI revenue by 2030 or they’ve wasted their capex.

from_speaker: at least $2 trillion in annual AI revenue
our_interpretation: The nearby discussion identifies Google, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle and SpaceX as the relevant hyperscalers.
The antecedent is failure to reach the stated annual revenue threshold by December 31, 2030.
The ordinary financial reading of 'wasted their capex' is failure to recover the investment and its financing costs, not that the assets produce no revenue.
The nearby 10% return calculation is context; the quoted claim does not explicitly make 10% its definition of waste.
Annual revenue means revenue earned over a year. An annualized monthly or quarterly run rate does not by itself establish that amount.
criteria.support_condition: If combined annual AI revenue fails to reach $2 trillion by the deadline, records must also show that the relevant AI capital investment failed to recover its costs. A revenue shortfall alone is insufficient.
criteria.contradiction_condition: If the revenue antecedent is met, reliable financial records show that the relevant AI capital investment recovered its costs despite annual AI revenue remaining below $2 trillion.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable annual AI revenue records through December 31, 2030 for the six specified companies. If revenue remains below $2 trillion, financial records and reproducible calculations must establish whether the identified AI investment recovered its costs, including financing costs without double-counting. Earlier resolution requires an irreversible event fixing both questions for the entire investment cohort.
